name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 19 points
Biss has raised $2.9M while the Republican shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%
Open seat with no general-election polling adds modest uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's nineteen-point Democratic lean, Biss's dominant fundraising against a Republican with no visible financial operation, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win near 98% all point to the seat staying safely in Democratic hands despite the open-seat dynamic.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Biss or an unexpected Republican fundraising surge could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement leaves an open seat in a Chicago-area district that has leaned Democratic by roughly nineteen points in recent elections. Daniel Biss, a well-known former state legislator and Evanston mayor, enters as the Democratic nominee with about $2.9 million raised and substantial outside spending both supporting and opposing him. Republican John Elleson shows no reported fundraising, leaving a wide financial gap.

No general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near certainty. The open-seat nature adds some uncertainty, but the district's partisan lean, Biss's name recognition and money, and the absence of a competitive Republican operation point to the seat remaining in Democratic hands with a margin in the low twenties.
